mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) above 2.5% over two consecutive months signals a tightening cycle, raising discount rates and compressing equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when this trigger is met.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1 growth) of more than -0.5% coincident with a rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 4% signals weakening aggregate demand, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 3.5% for three consecutive months, with no concurrent rise in average hourly earnings (implied by stable PAYEMS and INDPRO), indicates labor market softening, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE > 3.5% for three consecutive months AND (PAYEMS growth flat AND INDPRO growth flat)
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly below zero (t-test p > 0.10) during triggered periods.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in industrial production (INDPRO) of more than -1.0% for four consecutive months signals contraction in manufacturing output, which historically precedes negative equity returns over the next 20 trading days due to earnings downgrades.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp month-on-month decline in housing starts (HOUST) below 1,000,000 units, coincident with a rise in mortgage rates (implied by FEDFUNDS trajectory), signals a housing demand shock that negatively impacts consumer confidence and equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) during triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A prolonged period (six months) where the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) remains near zero or negative, in the absence of significant inflation (CPIAUCSL < 2.0%), signals a liquidity trap environment, which historically correlates with muted but positive equity returns over the next 60 trading days due to search-for-yield effects.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS <= 0% for six months AND CPIAUCSL < 2.0%
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly above zero (t-test p > 0.10) during triggered periods.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid acceleration in payroll employment growth (PAYEMS) above 0.5% month-over-month, accompanied by a stable unemployment rate (UNRATE), signals a tight labor market that boosts wage pressure and consumer spending, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) in triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained annualized GDP growth (GDPC1) above 3.0% for three consecutive quarters, with stable inflation (CPIAUCSL change < 0.2% month-over-month), signals robust demand expansion, which typically precedes positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days due to earnings growth expectations.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 > 3.0% annualized for three consecutive quarters AND CPIAUCSL change < 0.2% month-over-month
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly above zero (t-test p > 0.05) during triggered periods.
